title: Splitting a multi-arm trial's adjusted contrasts is conservative for one contrast and anticonservative for another
question: When a three-arm trial's population-adjusted contrasts share an arm and a weight vector, what is lost by treating them as independent, is the error ever anticonservative, and is dropping the trial cheaper?
answer: Ignoring the within-trial covariance errs in a direction set by the contrast, not by how the arms' effect modification aligns. The trial's own B-versus-C interval became conservative in every scenario, while the network A-versus-B interval, which borrows through the trial, fell below nominal in 15 of 30 scenarios. The shared-weighting part of the covariance took both signs but never reversed a contrast's error. Dropping the trial widened the network interval by 29% to 91%.
findings: Split, trial-alone d_BC: coverage 0.957 to 1.000, above nominal beyond 3 MCSE in 29 of 30 scenarios and below in none; DESIGN.md's alignment-sign prediction is withdrawn by its registered test.
Split, network d_AB: coverage 0.4 to 3.7 points below the stacked sandwich, below nominal beyond 3 MCSE in 15 of 30 scenarios against 0 for the stacked sandwich.
The shared-weighting covariance term was -22% to +15% of the Monte Carlo covariance, dominated by the shared-arm term.
Joint sandwiches recovered 0.76 to 1.15 (stacked) and 0.73 to 1.12 (weights fixed) of the Monte Carlo covariance; stacked trial-alone intervals covered 0.919 to 0.960.
Dropping the trial was unbiased and widened the network d_AB interval by a median 53%.
not_answered: Continuous outcome, linear modification, one three-arm trial in a fixed two-trial aggregate network; four-arm trials, the one-stage ML-NMR comparator and a bootstrap are not run, and target moments are fixed. Peer review has not been done.
design: Three-arm individual-data trial weighted by MAIC to a target, plus aggregate A-versus-C and B-versus-C trials in the target; 30 scenarios crossing effect-modification strength, its alignment across arms, target shift and shared-arm size; split, weights-fixed, stacked and drop analyses, network by generalized least squares.
estimand: d_AB, d_AC and d_BC in the target population
